name: Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite CPAP Battery
summary: The battery to pack for flights and backpacking; measure your draw, and buy two if one will not cover a night.
verdict: Medistrom builds the Pilot-24 Lite specifically for CPAP machines, and its main selling point is a capacity rated just under the 100 watt-hour line that most airlines and the FAA treat as the no-paperwork limit for carry-on lithium batteries. It outputs DC directly, so there is no inverter wasting a slice of the battery, and it uses a cable matched to your machine model, so check the compatibility list for your exact CPAP before buying. How long it lasts depends heavily on your draw: at low pressures with humidification and heated tubing off, some machines sip little enough for a full night, while at an average of 25 watts the math works out to about three and a half hours, so measure before you trust it. Medistrom also makes a 12-volt version, the Pilot-12 Lite, for machines that run on 12V; buying the wrong one is the most common mistake. Two Pilot-24 Lite packs are still airline-legal as spares in most cases, which is the cleanest way to cover a two-night trip.
skipIf: A full night is realistic only at low draw with the humidifier off
pros: Rated just under 100Wh, so no airline approval is needed
DC output avoids inverter losses entirely
Small enough to pack in a CPAP travel bag
Model-specific cables for widely used ResMed and Philips machines
USB port for a phone in the tent or hotel
cons: A full night is realistic only at low draw with the humidifier off
Requires the correct machine-specific cable, sold separately for some models
Expensive per watt-hour compared with a power station
